subject: general
question: Manoj has 200 litres of Oil A and 274 litres of Oil B. He fills a number of identical containers with the two types of oil in a manner that each container has only one type of oil, and all containers are completely filled. What can be the maximum volume (in litres) of each container that Manoj uses, so that all the oil that Manoj has, of both the types, can be poured into these containers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum volume** of identical containers, we must calculate the **HCF (Highest Common Factor)** of the given quantities.

Quantity of **Oil A** = 200 litres

Quantity of **Oil B** = 274 litres

HCF(200, 274) = 2 (Since 274 is not divisible by 4, 5, 8, or 10).

**∴ The correct answer is 2 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of **Oil A** = 200 litres

Volume of **Oil B** = 274 litres

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37131e27c9859fe0d606a71533400b6240d168b58f39ec1a7484020b84d481df.png] 

**Calculation:**

Using **Prime Factorization**:

⇒ 200 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 = 2³ × 5²

⇒ 274 = 2 × 137

⇒ Common Factor = 2

⇒ **HCF(200, 274)** = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

HCF is the greatest number which exactly divides two or more given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. Formula: Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.

Number of Containers

To find the minimum number of containers required: Total Quantity ÷ HCF value.</p
